arxiv_hits_found.title: ALP-mediated inelastic dark matter and the LUX-ZEPLIN high-recoil candidate event LZ230616
arxiv_hits_found.summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Collaboration has reported a high-energy candidate event LZ230616 with a reconstructed nuclear recoil energy $E_R=248\pm23_{\rm stat}\pm23_{\rm sys}~{\rm keV}$. We investigate a possible interpretation in terms of inelastic scattering between two Majorana dark matter states mediated by an axionlike particle coupled to gluons. The positive mass splitting suppresses low-energy recoils, while the momentum dependence of the interaction reshapes the high-energy spectrum. We treat the dark-sector and gluonic couplings independently and retain the momentum-dependent nucleon form factors and xenon nuclear responses. Using an approximate single-event likelihood, we find that, for $m_a=0.3~{\rm GeV}$, a narrow spectrum near the candidate energy arises at $m_χ\simeq0.35~{\rm TeV}$ and $δ\simeq330~{\rm keV}$, although this configuration requires a large coupling product and is highly sensitive to the Galactic halo speed cutoff. Our analysis establishes the kinematic and coupling requirements for subsequent tests using the thermal relic abundance and laboratory constraints on the mediator.

arxiv_hits_found.title: Heavy Sterile Fermions from the Atmosphere: LZ Limits on Neutrino Up-Scattering
arxiv_hits_found.summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has recently reported data extending to nuclear-recoil energies of about 270 keV, including a single event at 248 keV in a nearly background-free region, for an exposure of 2.84 tonne-years. We examine this dataset through neutrino up-scattering to a heavy sterile fermion induced by atmospheric neutrinos, mediated by vector, axial-vector, scalar and dipole interactions. Our main result is a set of constraints: using the part of the LZ data where no excess is observed, we obtain new bounds on all four scenarios that probe regions of parameter space not tested before, and show that dark matter detectors can provide competitive limits on neutrino up-scattering for sterile fermion masses above $\sim 50$ MeV. We also test whether the 248~keV event can be explained in this way while remaining consistent with the absence of events at lower recoil energies. For the scalar, vector and axial mediators this requires couplings at the edge of perturbativity, while the dipole does not provide a good fit, so we conclude that up-scattering is not a compelling explanation of the event.

arxiv_hits_found.title: Inelastic from the Other Side: Xenon Excitation Signals in Light of the LZ High-Recoil Event
arxiv_hits_found.summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment recently reported a single event consistent with a nuclear recoil of $E_{\rm NR}\sim248\pm23\,(\mathrm{stat})\pm23\,(\mathrm{syst})$~keV in an extended-energy search. We study the accompanying inelastic-xenon channel, $χ+\Xe\toχ+\Xe^{*}$, which provides a complementary test of DM interpretations of such high-recoil events. Using the non-relativistic effective-field-theory (NREFT) framework with shell-model nuclear-transition inputs, we compute the inelastic-xenon rates for representative scenarios including inelastic dark matter and accelerated DM populations. We also simulate their S1--S2 responses, with detector modeling validated against public LZ data. The nuclear de-excitation adds an electromagnetic component shifting the signal toward the electronic-recoil band and, in some cases, toward clustered backgrounds from isotopes. We therefore construct a schematic, physics-motivated background model and perform a simplified statistical analysis. For many benchmarks, the inelastic-xenon rate is $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ of the elastic rate or below, suggesting that substantially larger exposures are required before this companion channel becomes observable. Our results illustrate the importance of isotope-induced background structures in the extended-energy region and extend the phenomenology of inelastic-xenon signatures to a wider range of DM scenarios.

arxiv_hits_found.title: Atmospheric neutrino up-scattering explanation of LZ 2026 excess
arxiv_hits_found.summary: The recent observation of an isolated nuclear recoil at $248\pm 23\pm 23$ keV energy by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has motivated the community to look for a new physics explanation, as the Standard Model background estimation fails to accommodate it. Most of the existing literature hitherto considers a galactic halo dark matter with a heavier partner. In this work, we traverse the alternate route of atmospheric neutrino ($ν$) up-scattering, thus producing a massive beyond standard model (BSM) particle $χ$ with mass $m_χ$. The kinematic requirement of such a scattering demands a higher energy of the incoming neutrinos than elastic scattering, explaining the absence of excess events from solar $ν$ scattering. However, for high energy neutrinos in the tail of the atmospheric neutrino flux, the kinematic threshold no longer prevents events at low recoil energies. To avoid an excess of such events, we consider a momentum dependent operator, which suppresses the event rate at low recoil energies and allows a single event in the high recoil energy window. Such up-scattering on nuclei ($\mathcal{N}$), $ν\mathcal{N}\to χ\mathcal{N}$, can be naturally realized in sterile neutrino models, though we keep our analysis generic without specifying $χ$. We identify the region of parameter space that can produce such an isolated event, assuming a pseudoscalar mediator with mass $m_φ$ that couples to the $ν$-$χ$ pair with strength $y_χ$ and to up quarks with strength $y_u$. For example, $m_χ\simeq 1.13$~GeV, $m_φ\simeq 494$~MeV and $\sqrt{y_χy_u} \simeq 0.33$ can account for the observed event while remaining allowed by other existing constraints.
